questions.title: Cyclin-dependent kinases as internal cell cycle signals
questions.subject: fnd
questions.question: Which of the following is considered one of the internal signals that tightly regulate progression through the cell cycle?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Growth factors are external (extracellular) signals that influence whether a cell enters the cycle at all, not the internal molecular machinery that drives progression once the cycle is underway.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cytokines are extracellular signalling molecules, typically involved in immune communication, not the internal regulatory machinery of the cell cycle itself.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Environmental stresses are external factors that can trigger checkpoint arrest, but they are not themselves the internal regulatory signal that drives normal cycle progression.
explanations.D: Correct. Cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs), activated by binding their partner cyclins, are the internal molecular signal that phosphorylates target proteins and drives the cell past successive checkpoints through G1, S, G2 and M — the cell's own built-in progression machinery, not an external cue. Because different cyclins peak at different times, sequential cyclin-CDK complexes impose an ordered, one-way progression through the cycle's stages.

questions.learning_objective: State that cyclin-dependent kinases are internal regulators of cell cycle progression, activated only when bound to their partner cyclin, and that sequential cyclin-CDK complexes drive the cell through successive checkpoints.
